content.title: Tyson Fury vs Arslanbek Makhmudov fight date, time, where to watch
content.text: April 8, 2026, 5:04 a.m. CTAfter a brief retirement, Tyson Fury is returning to boxing as he takes on heavyweight contender Arslanbek Makhmudov.The bout is scheduled for April 11 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.Fury is coming off two consecutive losses to Oleksandr Usyk which spurred his retirement.Tyson Fury's brief retirement from boxing comes to a close on April 11 in London when he returns to the ring against towering heavyweight contender Arslanbek Makhmudov.Fury, a former lineal heavyweight champion, originally announced his retirement from the sport in January 2025 following consecutive defeats to unified titleholder and pound-for-pound No. 1 Oleksandr Usyk.It wasn't Fury's first time stepping away from the sport though, and to the surprise of few, his return was announced just over a year later."Since I retired for the fifth time over a year ago, boxing for me has gone on a downward slope. It's become quite boring and boxing is at its maximum potential when Tyson Fury's actively fighting….so believe it and I'm coming back to make boxing great again."There has been much speculation regarding a potential blockbuster all-English clash between Fury and Anthony Joshua later this year, but first Fury must get past the 6-foot-5½ Makhmudov, who's coming off two victories in 2025.Here's all you need to know ahead of the Fury vs. Makhmudov fight card.Where to watch Tyson Fury vs Makhmudov fightTyson Fury's comeback fight against Arslanbek Makhmudov and the accompanying undercard will air live on Netflix, at no extra cost to subscribers.How to watch: NetflixTyson Fury next fight: Fight date, timeCoverage of the Fury vs. Makhmudov headlined fight card will begin on Netflix at 1 p.m. (CT) on April 11. Ring walks for the main event are expected at approximately 4 p.m. (CT).Fight card start: 1 p.m. CTFury vs. Makhmudov ring walks: approx. 4 p.m. CTTyson Fury vs Makhmudov undercardThe undercard to Fury vs. Makhmudov sees the return of fellow British star Conor Benn, fresh off a unanimous decision victory over Chris Eubank Jr. in the same venue last November.Tyson Fury (34-2-1, 24 KOs) vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov (21-2, 19 KOs)Conor Benn (24-1, 14 KOs) vs. Regis Prograis (30-3, 24 KOs)Richard Riakporhe (19-1, 15 KOs) vs. Jeamie Tshikeva (9-2, 5 KOs)Frazer Clarke (9-2-1, 7 KOs) vs. Justis Huni (12-1, 7 KOs)Tyson Fury vs Makhmudov fight locationThe Tyson Fury vs. Arslanbek Makhmudov fight card will be held at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Fury previously fought Derek Chisora in the same venue in 2022, while it more recently hosted the first and second bouts between Benn and Eubank Jr.Location: Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London, UKTyson Fury recordTyson Fury is 34-2-1 with 24 wins by knockout.Fury reigned as lineal heavyweight champion for nearly a decade before suffering consecutive defeats to Usyk, first in a battle for the undisputed title. He'd previously held the WBC belt for four years, successfully defending three times while also defeating Francis Ngannou in a non-title bout.As he's returning from retirement, Fury is unranked at heavyweight.Tyson Fury weight, heightTyson Fury is 37 years old and stands at 6-foot-9 with an 85-inch reach. Fury has spent his entire career at heavyweight, weighting in at an average of 273.5 pounds across his last three bouts.Arslanbek Makhmudov recordArslanbek Makhmudov is 21-2 with 19 wins by knockout.Makhmudov is riding a two-fight win streak, most recently defeating British journeyman David Allen by unanimous decision last October. His two career defeats came in a three-fight span between 2023 and 2024, as he was stopped by both Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello.Makhmudov is a top-15 ranked contender with the IBF and WBA.Arslanbek Makhmudov weight, heightArslanbek Makhmudov is 36 years old and stands at 6-foot-5½ with a 72-inch reach. Makhmudov is a career heavyweight and has weighed in at an average of just over 262 pounds across his last three bouts.Tyson Fury highlightsHarrison Campbell covers combat sports for The Tennessean and high school sports for The Daily Herald.
